target.title: fix: render complete HTML entity set in agent workflows
target.body:
Closes #105897

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent workflows that consume HTML would leave most named HTML5 entities—such as `—`, `©`, and `…`—visible instead of rendering their characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the maintained `entities@8.0.0` decoder behind the shared agent HTML utility, then route web fetch, syntax highlighting, and provider tool-argument repair through that utility. The decoder keeps OpenClaw's existing single-pass, strict-numeric, invalid-reference, and legacy five-name case behavior; the web-fetch tokenizer is intentionally unchanged.

## User Impact

Fetched pages, highlighted HTML, and repaired provider tool arguments now render the full HTML5 named-entity set. Astral numeric entities remain intact, escaped entity-looking text is not decoded twice, and invalid numeric references remain literal.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcqwz4q680vvttx7sr20nen`: clean frozen install confirmed `entities@8.0.0`; focused decoder/caller suites passed 51 tests.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm test src/agents` passed 15,067 tests across 884 files (4 skipped).
- Same Testbox: `pnpm build` and `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --check` passed.
- Black-box behavior contract passed full named entities, exact-name precedence, mixed-case legacy names, astral numeric references, direct numeric compatibility, single-pass decoding, and invalid-reference preservation.
- Fresh branch autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- `pnpm check:changed` reaches the repository-wide TypeScript LOC ratchet and fails on unchanged `main` rows; the same failure was reproduced from the untouched base. The touched `web-fetch-utils.ts` row shrinks from 701 to 677 lines.
